name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
title: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in MCP servers and agent tooling, where the components that connect models to outside systems keep their own logs. The three CVEs here are OpenPanel 2.3.0, dbt-mcp before 1.17.1, and the AWS Bedrock AgentCore SDK 1.4.8 and 1.5.0. The sensitive data reaches the log through ordinary operation rather than any clever attack, because the product writes it there itself: MCP auth tokens in plaintext, SQL queries and variables in plaintext to a file, and raw prompts and responses to CloudWatch. Anyone who can read those logs, including support staff or a compromised log store, can replay the tokens or read the queries and prompts. That turns routine logging into a quiet leak of credentials and user content.
description: The product writes sensitive information to a log file.

mitigations.description: Consider seriously the sensitivity of the information written into log files. Do not write secrets into the log files.
Remove debug log files before deploying the application into production.
Protect log files against unauthorized read/write.
Adjust configurations appropriately when software is transitioned from a debug state to production.

consequences.note: Logging sensitive user data, full path names, or system information often provides attackers with an additional, less-protected path to acquiring the information.
